newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity fixed-income manager Ives resigns.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity fixed-income manager Ives resigns.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Wednesday that fixed-income mutual fund manager Bob Ives, who oversaw four funds with assets totalling about $1.5 billion, has resigned.
"He's indicated that he did not wish to relocate with the fixed-income division," Fidelity spokesman Scott Beyerl said.
Fidelity plans to move its fixed-income and money market divisions from Boston and Dallas to Merrimack, N.H. by August this year and Ives chose not to make the move, Beyerl said.
Beyerl said Ives has not indicated his future plans.

Ives, who joined Fidelity in 1991, was the manager of Fidelity Advisor Annuity Government Investment, Fidelity Advisor Government Investment, the $972.5 million Fidelity Government Securities and $277 million Fidelity Spartan Government Income.
Ives' fixed-income colleague Michael Gray, who managed or co-managed nine funds with assets of around $10 billion, resigned earlier this month to start his own firm specializing in fixed-income.
Sources told Reuters that Ives will join Gray at his new firm. When contacted by Reuters, Ives declined to comment.
Beyeryl said Fidelity will name a replacement for Ives in the next few days.
